title: Posted Schedule: The Hold Shrink Taken on Tickets Standing Held Against a Contract
content:
The hold shrink under Grain Marketing Contracts is taken on the credited bushels, because grain that sits in the elevator's hands before it is applied to a contract loses condition in handling.

| How long the tickets have stood held, and how they were probed | Hold shrink |
|---|---|
| Longer than 28 days, and two or more of them were probed above the moisture base | 0.75 percent |
| Longer than 14 days, but that pair of conditions is not met | 0.4 percent |
| Neither of those holds | none |

## The bands read at their edges

The long band asks for both of its conditions together: a hold running longer than 28 days, so that 28 days exactly is not long enough, and at least two tickets probed above the moisture base. A hold of 35 days with one conditioned ticket falls to the short band. The short band asks only that the hold has run longer than 14 days, so 15 days is inside it and 14 days is not.

| Days held | Tickets probed above the moisture base | Hold shrink |
|---|---|---|
| 40 | 3 | 0.75 percent |
| 40 | 1 | 0.4 percent |
| 28 | 3 | 0.4 percent |
| 15 | 0 | 0.4 percent |
| 14 | 5 | none |
| 9 | 2 | none |

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

Credited bushels of 10,000 on tickets held 32 days, two of them probed damp, are reduced by 0.75 percent to 9,925 bushels. The same bushels on tickets held 20 days are reduced by 0.4 percent to 9,960 bushels.
